title: Hamlet paper elevation research
scope: A proposed 2D architectural-elevation direction for an adult, warm town. This is visual research only, not an art decision or an application specification.
reference_policy: The accompanying board contains only newly drawn SVG shapes and colour swatches. It does not embed, copy, trace, or redistribute source artwork.

sources.title: Mega Mall Story — Kairosoft
sources.kind: official game page and official feature image
sources.reviewed: The official feature image was visually inspected on 2026-10-08.
observations: The mall is read as a stack of shallow room bands with one strong floor line per level.
A very small cast still reads because each room has one obvious action or object cluster.
Escalators, storefronts and the roadside establish program before ornament; the cross-section remains legible at a glance.
sources.take: Borrow the hierarchy of room bands and visible life; do not borrow pixels, UI, shop labels, commercial-game density, or its saturated outline treatment.

sources.title: Townscaper
sources.kind: official site and official key art
sources.reviewed: The official key art was visually inspected on 2026-10-08. The site states that placement creates houses, arches, stairways, bridges and backyards from configurations on an irregular grid.
observations: Neighbouring facades use a limited grammar: a common roof line, simple window rhythm, restrained seams and gentle value changes.
Colour blocks differentiate neighbours without needing a unique silhouette for every building.
The graphic is coherent because detail stays subordinate to the large roof and wall shapes.
sources.take: Use a small facade grammar and repeat it with controlled variation. Hamlet keeps its own square placement logic and its own adult paper-and-ink material.

sources.title: Brutal East II: Build Your Own Concrete Eastern Bloc
sources.reviewed: The official page describes nine pre-cut and pre-folded cardboard models and shows product/model imagery.
observations: A paper object reads through intentional side faces, fold lines, tabs and a small cast shadow rather than through noisy texture.
The difference between a front plane and a return plane is enough to make a compact facade feel made, not flat.
A construction grammar can stay clear when each fold earns a structural role.
sources.take: Use two or three shallow paper planes per building and one consistent lower-right cast shadow. Avoid literal craft tabs in the product view unless they help navigation.

sources.title: (w)Ego: The (w)Ego Game
sources.reviewed: The source preview describes a longitudinal section with interconnected rooms, stairs, furniture and human silhouettes in colour-coded zones.
observations: A cutaway is understood when circulation makes the spaces relate, not merely when rooms are exposed.
Small human figures reveal the intended scale of stairs, furniture and openings.
Room colour can organise program, but needs quiet shared structure to avoid becoming a diagram.
sources.take: Use a visible stair or street connection between rooms, a shared baseline, and people as scale checks; keep Hamlet's palette calm and its rooms purposeful.

direction.name: Paper street elevation
direction.one_sentence: A front-on, modular town street whose cutaway rooms sit behind refined inked facades, as though shallow painted paper architecture has been pinned onto a cream drawing sheet.
graphic_clarity: Work from a 24 px structural unit at 1×: frontages are 4–7 units wide, room floors 4 units tall, doors 1.5 units wide and windows 1 unit square.
Every building gets one silhouette cue: pitched roof, stepped parapet, wide awning, corner tower, or a tall entry. Do not combine more than two cues on one small facade.
Keep one dark ink (#33464A) for structure. Use 2 px exterior outlines, 1.25 px interior lines, and no more than one dashed construction/fold line per building.
Make the section readable in this order: roof/silhouette, room band, door/window, one active resident, then ornament. If an element does not survive at phone size, remove it.
material_rules: Use flat fills with sparse, hand-drawn line texture: at most 3 short marks per large surface. Do not use a global noise filter or photoreal paper texture.
Use a single light direction from upper left. Returns are 12–16% darker; cast shadows are ink at 14% opacity, offset 5 px right and 7 px down at 1×.
Paper depth stays shallow: facade plane 0, return plane +6 px, roof plane +10 px. The town should remain an elevation, not pretend to be 3D isometric art.
Reserve lamp gold for interiors and tiny street lamps. At night, darken paper and road slightly but preserve the ink contrast.
facade_and_room_rules: Build from three reusable modules: facade shell, interior room inset, and foreground/sidewalk prop strip. Keep them separately drawable and movable.
Show one room story per bay: a desk and seated figure, a counter and standing figure, or a letter table and delivery figure. Three props maximum before the room becomes a dollhouse inventory.
Windows should align to the structural grid, while awnings, plants and signage can break it slightly. This keeps the town hand-made without losing placement clarity.
Use closed facades for most buildings; open just one or two cutaway rooms in the initial street. The alternation makes open interiors feel special and preserves visual rest.
inhabitant_scale: A standing inhabitant is 0.72 of the clear floor height; its head should sit below the window head and its feet exactly on the room baseline.
Use simple round or bean-like heads, two legs and one gesture. Faces are optional below 18 px tall; posture and prop should carry the action.
Place at most three inhabitants in any uninterrupted 160 px street span. Every person must either show scale, suggest a task, or indicate a route.
street_organisation: Use three constant horizontal bands: building plinth, 18–22 px pedestrian pavement, and 34–42 px shared lane. Repeated bands make the town rearrangeable.
Make the curb line continuous across building modules. A road segment never terminates at a facade; it turns at a visible corner module or leaves the frame.
Use a teal delivery van or coral bicycle sparingly as a moving accent. It must sit in the lane, never overlap the pavement or room band.
Cluster planting, mailbox and lamp props at seams between buildings. They soften joins and offer rhythm without disguising the grid.
direction.first_art_test: Draw one 6-unit news-and-post facade, one 5-unit home cutaway, a 10-unit road run, two inhabitants, one lamp and one van. Review it at actual phone size in day and night before extending the kit.
